  • Persistence, Outputs, and Data I/O

Persistence, Outputs, and Data I/O

RELIC provides three distinct persistence layers:

  1. StateManager snapshots for in-memory transactional restore.

  2. RELICSimulator checkpoints for runtime continuation.

  3. Data and provenance writers for durable scientific outputs.

These layers serve different contracts and are not interchangeable.

State snapshots

StateManager.checkpoint() returns an in-memory mapping containing state tensors, counters, diagnostics, history, conservation records, and pending provenance transaction data. restore(snapshot) accepts only a valid mapping produced by that state manager contract.

import torch

from relic.core.state import StateManager
from relic.core.state.types import StateVariableSpec, UpdateItem, UpdateMode

manager = StateManager(
    {"x": StateVariableSpec(name="x", units="dimensionless")}
)
manager.initialize({"x": torch.tensor(1.0)})

snapshot = manager.checkpoint()
manager.apply_updates(
    {
        "x": UpdateItem(
            value=torch.tensor(1.0),
            mode=UpdateMode.ACCUMULATE,
            unit="dimensionless",
            per_timestep=True,
        )
    },
    check_conservation=False,
)
manager.restore(snapshot)

print(float(manager.get_state()["x"]))

Expected output:

1.0

restore() raises TypeError for a non-mapping snapshot and ValueError when the required state mapping is absent. Use snapshots around local transactions; they are not a stable cross-version file format.

Simulator checkpoints

RELICSimulator.create_checkpoint(
    checkpoint_path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    snapshot: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

RELICSimulator.restore_checkpoint(
    checkpoint_path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    compatibility_certificate: RestartCompatibilityCertificate | None = None,
    migration_certificate: GraphMigrationCertificate | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

relic\core\simulator\checkpoint.py is the sole owner of the durable checkpoint format. Without snapshot, the public create call captures the live state and requires an explicit, non-existing target path; an existing file raises FileExistsError. It creates parent directories, writes a unique sibling temporary file, and atomically commits the target. snapshot is a frozen checkpoint payload captured at an accepted step boundary for a checkpoint delivery: it is written as given and never rebuilt from live state, and an existing target is accepted only when its verified payload is identical, in which case the receipt is returned again; a different file raises FileExistsError. The call never selects an implicit output directory and never overwrites an existing checkpoint.

from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import torch

from relic.core.dependency_graph import DependencyGraphResolver
from relic.core.simulator import RELICSimulator
from relic.core.state import StateManager
from relic.core.state.types import StateVariableSpec
from relic.scientific.atmosphere.stochastic_temperature import (
    OrnsteinUhlenbeckTemperatureFunctor,
)


def build_stochastic_simulator(seed: int) -> RELICSimulator:
    state_mgr = StateManager(
        {
            "stochastic_air_temperature_anomaly": StateVariableSpec(
                name="stochastic_air_temperature_anomaly",
                units="K",
            )
        },
        device=torch.device("cpu"),
    )
    state_mgr.initialize(
        {"stochastic_air_temperature_anomaly": torch.tensor([0.5], dtype=torch.float64)}
    )
    sim = RELICSimulator(
        {"time_step": 3600.0, "device": "cpu", "conservation_checks": False}
    )
    sim.initialize(state_mgr, DependencyGraphResolver())
    sim.register_functor(
        OrnsteinUhlenbeckTemperatureFunctor(config={"seed": seed}),
        execution_group="fast",
    )
    return sim


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    checkpoint_path = Path(tmpdir) / "restart" / "step_000001.pt"
    simulator = build_stochastic_simulator(seed=42)
    simulator.step(3600.0)
    create_receipt = simulator.create_checkpoint(checkpoint_path)
    simulator.step(3600.0)
    continuous_val = float(
        simulator.get_state()["stochastic_air_temperature_anomaly"].detach()[0]
    )

    restored_simulator = build_stochastic_simulator(seed=42)
    restore_receipt = restored_simulator.restore_checkpoint(checkpoint_path)
    restored_simulator.step(3600.0)
    restarted_val = float(
        restored_simulator.get_state()["stochastic_air_temperature_anomaly"].detach()[0]
    )
    print(create_receipt["sha256"] == restore_receipt["sha256"])
    print(continuous_val == restarted_val)

Both operations return path, format_version, size_bytes, file sha256, canonical payload_sha256, and provider_epoch. Creation leaves provider_epoch=None; a successful restore reports the newly committed view epoch. Automatic checkpoint names are checkpoint_directory/<run_id>/checkpoint_step_<12-digit-step>.pt. run_id belongs to the simulator, survives restart, and changes on reset.

Format 3 includes the frozen delivery_state: accepted pending obligations, receipts, job definitions, and flat checkpoint-node references. Restoring a checkpoint reconciles accepted notifications and delivery work through the existing owners; it does not recapture newer live outputs or deliver effects during state restoration. Retry retains each original run and destination. Delivery is at-least-once: every obligation carries an idempotency key and a receipt, so redelivery to an idempotent consumer is effectively-once. Cross-system exactly-once delivery requires the counterpart to take part in the protocol and is not claimed. Only obligations present in the persisted checkpoint are durably recoverable.

The versioned relic.simulator.checkpoint payload contains:

  • simulator time, counters, configuration-relevant runtime fields, and output history;

  • one validated in-memory StateManager.checkpoint() snapshot;

  • every registered Functor’s {state_dict, parameter_bindings} entry: standard PyTorch module state (including safe get_extra_state() data) and live values of manager bindings held by reference, including nested Functors;

  • Functor topology, dependency order/groups, StateManager schema, scientific configuration/metadata/parameter contracts, resolved devices, and distributed rank/world-size signature;

  • Python, Torch CPU, optional legacy global NumPy, and CUDA random number generator (RNG) states;

  • a canonical payload Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit (SHA-256) integrity record.

Restore uses torch.load(..., map_location="cpu", weights_only=True), requires the exact relic.simulator.checkpoint format and format_version=3, and has no unsafe deserialization fallback. Only version 3 is written. A version-2 file is upgraded in memory: held bindings move from module state into parameter_bindings; an unknown state entry raises ValueError. The upgraded payload is resealed and validated, and format_upgrade in the restore receipt records from_format_version, to_format_version, and moved_bindings. Binding restore requires matching key sets, shape, and dtype and preserves the live object, gradient flag, and device. CUDA RNG presence must match the resolved runtime symmetrically, including the CUDA device count; when pinning RELICSimulator to "device": "cpu" on a CUDA-capable host, pass device=torch.device("cpu") to an externally constructed StateManager so both owners resolve CPU tensors symmetrically. The current single-file format fails closed on both create and restore when an active distributed runtime has world_size > 1.

Restore requires a prepared, compatible simulator. It validates payload integrity, topology, scientific contracts, devices, distributed context, StateManager state, Functor state dictionaries, and RNG data before applying the restart. A failure before provider-view publication restores the pre-restore runtime fields, StateManager, Functor state, RNG, accepted pending work, and registration metadata. Once the new provider view is published, its epoch and scientific state remain committed even if retirement, cleanup, or receipt I/O fails; that error is reported as post-publication failure and must not rewind a world that readers may already have observed.

A checkpoint does not capture the state of external services or data sources. An external adapter stores only its source and model binding (get_extra_state()), and restoring that binding into an adapter bound to another source or model raises ValueError. Its opened datasets are not part of the checkpoint; a restarted run opens them again through discover() and open(). Adapter forward(state, time, dt, *, calendar_type, time_origin) selects forcing at time_origin + time using its declared time_interpolation; it does not own a separate mutable time cursor. An explicitly bound forcing sequence has the simulator-owned cursor, which advances only on accepted steps and is restored by the checkpoint.

The default restore is exact. The same owner accepts a RestartCompatibilityCertificate for bounded declared contract/parameter differences and state renames that preserve units, shape, and dtype. It binds the actual source and target topology digests; it cannot waive kernel, implementation, Functor-type, execution-order, or runtime-environment changes. Its forcing policy either preserves the exact cursor or explicitly clears it. GraphMigrationCertificate handles declared renaming/addition/retirement in its restricted graph family, including history requirements and mapped owners. The two certificate arguments are mutually exclusive. Neither provides arbitrary code equivalence, unit conversion, or shape migration.

StateManager.checkpoint() remains an in-memory transaction primitive. It is embedded in the durable simulator payload but is not an independent file format or a second persistence owner. Likewise, Functors use state_dict()/load_state_dict() and PyTorch get_extra_state()/set_extra_state() without introducing a parallel restart API. Stochastic Functors built on FunctorSubstreamMixin, including OrnsteinUhlenbeckTemperatureFunctor (relic.scientific.atmosphere.stochastic_temperature) and MarkedPoissonRainfallFunctor (relic.scientific.atmosphere.stochastic_rainfall), persist their Wiener or marked-jump substream cursor in extra_state, so accepted-step rollback and restore_checkpoint() replay the identical stochastic sample path. Manager bindings held by reference are outside module state; the same checkpoint owner captures and restores them through parameter_bindings.

Automatic checkpoints are disabled by default. Enabling them requires all three runtime settings:

from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

from relic.core.simulator import RELICSimulator

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    simulator = RELICSimulator(
        {
            "enable_checkpointing": True,
            "checkpoint_directory": str(Path(tmpdir) / "automatic"),
            "checkpoint_frequency": 3600.0,
        }
    )
    print(simulator.enable_checkpointing)

The frequency must be positive. Automatic persistence occurs only after an accepted scientific and provenance step commit, using checkpoint_step_<12-digit-step>.pt in the explicit directory’s run_id subdirectory. File errors propagate, and there is no public checkpoint cleanup API.

A bitwise-equal uninterrupted run and split restart run is strong dynamic evidence only for the tested graph, inputs, fixed-step protocol, dependency stack, and device environment. It does not promise cross-platform, cross-version, cross-device, or multi-rank bitwise identity.

Run bundles

from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

from relic.orchestration import GraphIR, NodeRegistry, SSOTCatalog, compile_graph
from relic.orchestration.compiler import write_run_bundle

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    graph = GraphIR(
        schema_version="1.0",
        nodes={},
        metadata={"name": "bundle_demo"},
    )
    registry = NodeRegistry(SSOTCatalog.from_parameter_manager())
    plan = compile_graph(graph, registry, strict=True)
    artifacts = write_run_bundle(
        graph,
        plan,
        Path(tmpdir) / "run_bundle",
    )
    print(len(artifacts), "manifest" in artifacts)

write_run_bundle(
    graph: GraphIR,
    plan: ExecutionPlan,
    output_dir: pathlib.Path,
    *,
    run_id: str | None = None,
    input_files: list[pathlib.Path] | None = None,
    metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]

write_run_bundle is imported from relic.orchestration.compiler; the relic.orchestration package does not export it. graph must be the canonical GraphIR that plan was compiled from; another type raises TypeError and a different graph raises ValueError. run_id names the provenance run (default: the current UTC time, YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ). input_files lists the input files to hash; when it is omitted, graph.metadata["input_files"] is used. metadata adds caller entries to the bundle metadata; the keys schema_version and graph_metadata are reserved and raise ValueError.

The bundle records the declarative workflow, compile result, runtime log target, environment and repository evidence, input checksums when input files are declared, and W3C Provenance Data Model (PROV) metadata.

Artifact

Purpose

workflow.json

Serialized GraphIR.

execution_plan.json

Serialized execution steps.

compile_report.json

Validation, structural audit, adapters, and compile metadata.

runtime.log.jsonl

Runtime event stream target.

env_snapshot.txt

Execution-environment snapshot.

git_status.json

Repository-state evidence.

inputs_manifest.sha256

Hash manifest for declared input files.

prov.jsonld

Machine-readable provenance graph.

manifest.json

Run identity, metadata, and the path of every bundle artifact.

checksums.sha256

Hashes of the bundle files.

write_run_bundle() creates the target directory, verifies the sealed bundle, and returns normalized artifact paths. It raises TypeError if the provenance recorder does not return the required mapping.

Conservation diagnostic output

from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import torch

from relic.core.state import StateManager
from relic.core.state.types import StateVariableSpec, UpdateItem, UpdateMode
from relic.data.io.diagnostic_writer import export_diagnostics_to_netcdf

state_manager = StateManager(
    {
        "carbon_pool": StateVariableSpec(
            name="carbon_pool",
            units="kg C m-2",
            conserved=True,
            accumulates="carbon.total",
        )
    }
)
state_manager.initialize({"carbon_pool": torch.tensor(2.0)})
state_manager.apply_updates(
    {
        "carbon_pool": UpdateItem(
            value=torch.tensor(0.0),
            mode=UpdateMode.ACCUMULATE,
            unit="kg C m-2",
            per_timestep=True,
            element="carbon",
        )
    },
    dt=3600.0,
    check_conservation=True,
)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    diag_result = export_diagnostics_to_netcdf(
        summaries=state_manager.conservation_history,
        time_coords=[3600.0],
        output_path=Path(tmpdir) / "diagnostics.nc",
        reference_date="1850-01-01",
    )
    print(diag_result.validation_passed)

export_diagnostics_to_netcdf(
    summaries: list[ConservationSummary],
    time_coords: list[float],
    output_path: pathlib.Path,
    reference_date: str = "1850-01-01",
    *,
    delivery_key: Optional[str] = None,
    metadata_registry: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Any]]] = None,
) -> WriteResult

The writer converts conservation summaries to an xarray dataset and delegates Climate and Forecast (CF) attribute synchronization and output creation to DataWriter, without adding time bounds. It returns the WriteResult and raises OSError when the write or its output validation fails. metadata_registry replaces the default per-variable diagnostic metadata. delivery_key is stored as the global attribute relic_delivery_key, so a retried delivery with the same key and options keeps the original creation timestamp. summaries and time_coords must describe the same sequence of simulation steps.

DataIO

from relic.data.io import DataIO, ReadConfig, WriteConfig

io = DataIO(
    reader_config=ReadConfig(cf_validate=True, cf_standardize=True),
    writer_config=WriteConfig(cf_sync=True, validate_output=True),
)

DataIO(
    reader_config: Optional[ReadConfig] = None,
    writer_config: Optional[WriteConfig] = None,
)

Read configuration

ReadConfig field

Default

Meaning

format

AUTO

Detect the supported source format.

chunks

None

Optional xarray chunk mapping.

parallel

True

Enable supported parallel I/O behavior.

cache_size

128

Reader cache size in MB.

cf_validate

True

Check each variable’s explicit standard_name and units with CFConventions.validate_cf_compliance; the check runs only inside the cf_standardize step.

cf_standardize

True

Run the explicit-metadata CF step. It never renames variables, infers attributes, or changes values or units. With cf_validate, invalid metadata sets ReadResult.success and ReadResult.validation_passed to False, or raises ValueError when strict_cf is set. The step always adds a warning that dataset-level CF conformance was not evaluated.

strict_cf

False

Raise for metadata (CF standard-name and unit) findings; without it such findings are recorded and the result is marked failed. Every other failure (a failed processing pipeline, tensor conversion, write, chunking request or file close) raises in both modes; raw or partial data are never returned in its place.

process_time

True

Process time coordinates.

time_bounds

True

Compute missing time bounds where supported.

standard_calendar

False

Keep the source calendar. True accepts only gregorian and raises for any other calendar, because no cross-calendar conversion exists.

variables

None

Variables to include; None means all.

exclude_vars

None

Variables to exclude.

standard_names_only

False

Return only variables with standard-name support.

apply_unit_conversion

False

Convert CF-consistent variables to target_units or to the CF canonical unit of their standard_name (see below).

target_units

None

Variable-to-target-unit mapping; each unit must be CF-consistent with the variable’s standard_name.

file_path

None

Not read by the reader; pass the path to the read call.

True

Run data validation.

fill_missing

False

Fill supported missing coordinate data.

quality_flags

False

Accepted but not used; the reader adds no quality flags.

to_torch

False

Return a tensor mapping in place of an xarray dataset.

torch_dtype

torch.float32

Tensor output type.

torch_device

"cpu"

Tensor output device.

Unit conversion on read

With apply_unit_conversion=True, the reader converts each variable that has both units and standard_name attributes. The target is target_units[name] when given, otherwise the canonical unit of the standard name in the CF table. Variables without these attributes, or whose standard name defines no canonical unit, are left unchanged. The source and the target unit must both be CF-consistent with the standard name.

The values are converted only by the shared UnitConverter. It uses an explicit conversion rule when one exists; otherwise it converts a pair of units of the same dimension that differ only by a scale factor through UDUNITS, for example kg m-2 day-1 to kg m-2 s-1. Affine pairs without a rule, such as degF to K, and pairs of different dimensions still need an explicit rule. The reader passes an empty ConversionContext: it supplies no temperature, pressure, or density, so a conversion that needs one fails.

A converted variable keeps standard_name and its other attributes, gets the new units, and records the previous unit in original_units; a note is added to ReadResult.warnings. A variable with a CF-inconsistent unit, or one that cannot be converted, keeps its values and units, and the read is marked failed: ReadResult.success and ReadResult.validation_passed become False and the reason is added to warnings. With strict_cf=True the read raises ValueError instead. DataIO.read() returns only the data, so inspect the ReadResult from DataIO.reader.read_dataset(...) or convert_format(...), or set strict_cf=True.

Conversions of model state that need context take it from UnitConverter.get_conversion_context(state, *, layer_thickness_variable=None, layer_thickness=None, temperature=None, pressure=None). The layer thickness (the context field soil_depth, in m) comes only from the state variable that the converted variable declares as its layer thickness (the layer_thickness_variable of its variable contract, which the transport bridge reads), read pointwise, or from an explicit layer_thickness. Giving both raises ValueError, as does a named variable that is missing from state; no fixed state name such as soil_depth or root_zone_depth is looked up. Temperature is read only from air_temperature and pressure only from atmospheric_pressure; the alias air_pressure is resolved upstream by the ContractRegistry, and no other name is tried. A conversion that needs another temperature or pressure, such as a leaf or soil temperature, receives it through the explicit temperature [K] or pressure [Pa] argument, which takes precedence over the state. water_density is taken from state when present. State fields are kept as tensors. No default values are filled in: a field that stays None makes the conversion that needs it raise.

Read, write, and convert

from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import xarray as xr

from relic.data.io import DataIO, ReadConfig, WriteConfig

io = DataIO(
    reader_config=ReadConfig(cf_validate=True, cf_standardize=True),
    writer_config=WriteConfig(cf_sync=True, validate_output=True),
)
source_dataset = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "air_temperature": (
            ("time",),
            [288.15, 289.15],
            {"standard_name": "air_temperature", "units": "K"},
        ),
        "precipitation_flux": (
            ("time",),
            [1.0e-5, 2.0e-5],
            {"standard_name": "precipitation_flux", "units": "kg m-2 s-1"},
        ),
    },
    coords={
        "time": (
            ("time",),
            [0.0, 3600.0],
            {
                "standard_name": "time",
                "units": "seconds since 2000-01-01 00:00:00",
                "calendar": "noleap",
            },
        )
    },
)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    forcing_path = Path(tmpdir) / "forcing.nc"
    io.write(source_dataset, forcing_path, format="netcdf4")

    dataset = io.read(
        forcing_path,
        variables=["air_temperature", "precipitation_flux"],
    )
    tensors = io.read(
        forcing_path,
        variables=["air_temperature"],
        to_torch=True,
        torch_device="cpu",
    )
    write_result = io.write(
        dataset,
        Path(tmpdir) / "forcing_standardized.nc",
        format="netcdf4",
    )
    read_result, conversion_result = io.convert_format(
        forcing_path,
        Path(tmpdir) / "forcing.zarr",
        "zarr",
    )
    print(sorted(tensors), write_result.validation_passed, conversion_result.validation_passed)

Method

Return value

read(source, **kwargs)

xarray.Dataset or dict[str, Tensor]

read_variables(source, variables, **kwargs)

Variable mapping

read_tensors(source, variables, device="cpu", dtype=torch.float32)

Tensor mapping

write(data, output_path, **kwargs)

WriteResult

write_tensors(tensors, output_path, coordinates=None, metadata=None, **kwargs)

WriteResult

convert_format(source_path, target_path, target_format, **kwargs)

(ReadResult, WriteResult)

get_file_info(file_path)

File metadata mapping; a file whose metadata cannot be read raises (no mapping carrying an error entry).

ReadResult retains loaded data, metadata, CF and validation flags, warnings, timing, file size, time-processing status, and standardized-variable mappings. WriteResult reports the output path, size, timing, compression ratio, CF and validation flags, warnings, variables, coordinates, and computed bounds.

Interpret every CF result by its declared scope. The existing CFConventions.validate_cf_compliance(...) checks one variable’s official standard name and compatible units; it reports single_variable_standard_name_and_units, not whole-dataset conformance. CFConventions.validate_dataset_conformance(...) evaluates declared_dataset_scope: the Conventions declaration, units, official names, axis values, time units/calendar, coordinates and bounds references/shapes, missing-value consistency, and cell-method syntax/dimensions. Grid mappings, discrete sampling geometries, gathering compression, external variables, and group hierarchies are outside that scope. Name Table v94 membership cannot itself authorize a dataset Conventions declaration.

The external IOHandler.read(...) reports its dataset check through IOResult.cf_validation_scope, dataset_conformance_checked, and cf_conformance_issues; cf_compliant=True requires that the declared check actually ran and found no issue. Other result types and unchecked paths must not inherit this claim merely from a similarly named boolean field.

Supported read formats include NetCDF4, NetCDF3, HDF5, Zarr, and CSV. Supported write formats include NetCDF4, NetCDF3, Zarr, and CSV. A missing file raises FileNotFoundError; unsupported data or formats raise ValueError; strict CF violations raise ValueError.

For conversion overrides, prefix reader-only options with read_:

from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import xarray as xr

from relic.data.io import DataIO

io = DataIO()
sample = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "air_temperature": (
            ("time",),
            [288.15, 289.15],
            {"standard_name": "air_temperature", "units": "K"},
        )
    },
    coords={
        "time": (
            ("time",),
            [0.0, 3600.0],
            {
                "standard_name": "time",
                "units": "seconds since 2000-01-01 00:00:00",
                "calendar": "noleap",
            },
        )
    },
)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    src = Path(tmpdir) / "forcing.nc"
    dst = Path(tmpdir) / "forcing_subset.nc"
    io.write(sample, src, format="netcdf4")
    read_res, conv_res = io.convert_format(
        src,
        dst,
        "netcdf4",
        read_variables=["air_temperature"],
        compression="zstd",
        compression_level=6,
    )
    print(read_res.success, conv_res.validation_passed)

Experimental data quality and streaming gates

Two experimental data modules remain gated by explicit environment variables checked at import time:

  • relic.data.quality (QualityValidator, RangeRule, ValidationIssue) requires RELIC_EXPERIMENTAL_DATA_QUALITY=1 before import; otherwise require_experimental_feature raises RuntimeError.

  • relic.data.streaming requires RELIC_EXPERIMENTAL_STREAMING=1 before import; otherwise the exported names raise StreamingDisabledError (or RuntimeError).

Streaming windows

StreamWindow(
    size: timedelta,
    step: Optional[timedelta] = None,
    aggregation_method: str = "mean",
    quality_checks: bool = True,
)

Field

Meaning

size

Window length; a window is complete when the newest record is at least size after the window start. The reduced output is stamped at the window centre.

step

Advance of the window start; None uses size.

aggregation_method

Reduction over time: mean, sum, min, or max, written as cell_methods = "time: <method>". Any other value, including "MEAN", raises ValueError when the window is built.

quality_checks

Run quality control on each window.

The window has no coverage or gap fields; passing min_data_fraction or max_gap_duration raises TypeError. Coverage and gap limits come from the quality-control parameters coupling.scales.temporal.coverage_threshold and coupling.scales.temporal.quality_control.*.

With quality_checks=True, the window time series of each variable is checked before the reduction with QualityController.validate_for_operation(series, time_coord, "aggregation"). A series fails when its valid fraction is below the coverage threshold or its quality grade is below acceptable; the reduced variable then gets the attribute quality_flags = "validation_failed". A variable without a time dimension gets "not_assessed". A numeric time axis needs CF units and calendar attributes, and window data without a time dimension raises. Errors propagate to the stream consumer; a failed window is not dropped with a warning.

CF attributes after scaling

CFAttributeSynchronizer in relic.data.standards.cf_conventions carries explicit CF metadata through a processing step. It does not change or unit-convert the data tensor, and it does not infer units, variable roles, grids, or coordinates. Each sync_after_* method passes the data and metadata through CFConventions.sync_variable_attributes, which derives two metadata values from the data: shape (list(data.shape)) and, for non-empty data, actual_range ([float(data.min()), float(data.max())]). The range is [nan, nan] when the data contain NaN. For empty data actual_range is not written, so a value already in the input metadata is kept. The method-specific attributes in the table below are written on top of these two fields.

sync_variable_attributes first checks the standard name and units of the input metadata and raises ValueError for an issue even when strict_mode is False; the only exception is when every issue is an undefined unit contract for the standard name. With strict_mode=True, the updated metadata is checked again, and an issue found by this bounded CF check raises ValueError.

Method

Behavior

sync_after_aggregation(data, metadata, aggregation_method, dimension="time", *, source_label, target_label)

Sets the <dimension>: <method> cell method and appends Aggregated <dimension> from <source_label> to <target_label> (<dimension>: <method>) to history.

sync_after_disaggregation(data, metadata, disaggregation_method, dimension="area", *, source_label, target_label)

Same, with a Disaggregated ... entry. The allowed cell methods depend on dimension: sum (each fine cell holds its own total) or mean (each fine cell holds a mean) for area, and sum, mean, or point (instantaneous states) for time. Other methods and other dimensions raise ValueError.

sync_after_regridding(data, metadata, regrid_method, source_grid, target_grid)

Requires shape in both grids and a non-empty string for each name in CF_REGRID_TARGET_GRID_FIELDS (grid_mapping, lat_name, lon_name) in target_grid; writes grid_mapping and coordinates and appends a regridding entry to history.

sync_after_temporal_aggregation(data, metadata, time_coord, operation, method, coverage_stats, *, source_label, target_label)

Calls sync_after_aggregation (operation="aggregation") or sync_after_disaggregation (operation="disaggregation") with dimension="time". The variable keeps its standard_name, units, and long_name, gets the time: <method> cell method, and gains the history entry Aggregated time from <source_label> to <target_label> (time: <method>) (or Disaggregated time ...). Coverage fields come from the required coverage_stats (coverage_fraction, or valid_points and total_points): coverage_fraction, coverage_threshold read from coupling.scales.temporal.coverage_threshold, and quality_state (good_data or insufficient_coverage). The attributes of the result time coordinate are returned under time_coordinate, with bounds only when the coordinate has bounds; in strict mode only these time-coordinate attributes get the temporal check.

The source and target labels are required, non-empty scale labels such as "hourly" and "daily"; a missing or empty label raises.

Data I/O command checks

python -m relic.interfaces.cli.main data io check
python -m relic.interfaces.cli.main data io read data\forcing.nc
python -m relic.interfaces.cli.main data io convert data\forcing.nc output\forcing.zarr --target-format zarr

Use --help on the selected subcommand before an operation because format-specific arguments are command-specific.

data io check runs the I/O health checks. The I/O performance check is an error when its read or write benchmark fails (a failed memory benchmark lowers a healthy result to a warning); the streaming throughput check of the experimental data stream check is an error when a benchmark raises.
